proof_scope: The adjacent true cap-height change in the full masked observable at fixed ordinary repair depth equals the exact adjoint contraction in (1). It uses the true clipped-activation secant, both adjacent ordinary repair trajectories, their scalar negative-part slopes, and the exact masked coefficient with both true factors.

Under the actual critical cap rate, at fixed ordinary depth the slope supports have size O(sqrt n + n q_M^(2m)). At q_M^m=O(n^(-1/4)) the signed adjoint admits an exact sparse preimage with support O(sqrt n), maximum size O(n^(-1/2)) and normalized first norm O(n^(-1)). The image may be dense.

The signed sum of these actual cap-increment tests connects any controlled shorter endpoint to the true fixed-point statistic. The absolute tail past the explicit logarithmic cutoff costs O(n^(-kappa)) in nT. On the inherited obstruction, if the shorter endpoint also falls below one quarter of the positive lower, then an adjacent test before that cutoff has positive signed size at least c_*/(2(L-m_0)). The selected step can depend on the prime.
